sources.title: L2S2: chemical perturbation and CRISPR KO LINCS L1000 signature search engine
sources.depth: Primary abstract/introduction/data availability, authors' download-page source code at commit 42814c9c2bfc13ebebb05705fad937e389924682; not a full-paper re-review
sources.supports: A newer accessible collection has broad CRISPR and chemical coverage; motivates testing the older panel's BUB1B coverage gap.
sources.does_not_support: The published search engine's hit list is not evidence of rescue, and processing more signatures is not new biological replication. We use original Broad measured-landmark values, not this paper's inferred-gene search results.

sources.depth: Public data page, terms and complete four metadata tables; original matrices downloaded and integrity-checked by the campaign
sources.supports: Anonymous public metadata and original L1000 files; source page encourages publication of analytical findings.
sources.challenge: Source-file redistribution restrictions; data reuse across releases, compound stereochemistry and quality must be audited. No source-data relicensing or wholesale expression-file redistribution.

sources.title: Evaluation of RNAi and CRISPR technologies by large-scale gene expression profiling in the Connectivity Map
sources.depth: Carried-forward v23 primary-source review and deposited raw/PRIME data; no new full-paper review claimed
sources.supports: Orthogonal perturbation methods can expose RNAi attribution problems.
sources.challenge: The same RNAi experiments remain reused. New CRISPR data do not erase seed/batch concerns or establish functional equivalence between knockdown and knockout.

sources.title: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing induces a p53-mediated DNA damage response
sources.depth: Primary publisher abstract; full article not obtained
sources.supports: Editing itself can activate p53 and cell-cycle arrest in immortalized retinal pigment epithelial cells.
sources.challenge: This cannot quantify that effect in the LINCS cell lines; it requires an editing-stress control rather than explaining away every observed BUB1B signal.

sources.title: P53 independent pathogenic mechanisms contribute to BubR1 microcephaly
sources.depth: Primary abstract retrieved through Europe PMC; not a full-paper review
sources.supports: In the studied mouse cortex, Trp53 co-deletion leaves residual cell death and little anatomical rescue after BubR1 loss.
sources.challenge: Suppressing a downstream response is not sufficient evidence of functional rescue. Complete developmental loss in mice is not the selected human allele pair.

sources.title: Rapamycin Exerts Its Geroprotective Effects in the Ageing Human Immune System by Enhancing Resilience Against DNA Damage
sources.depth: Primary abstract retrieved through Europe PMC; indexed in v21 but not a new independent study; full methods and supplementary material not reviewed here
sources.supports: Favorable counterweight: the authors report lower DNA damage and better survival after acute genotoxic stress in human T cells, with a p21 change in an older-adult placebo-controlled study.
sources.challenge: These outcomes do not establish chromosome-segregation repair, pediatric safety, BUB1B-specific rescue or everolimus equivalence. They argue against a blanket claim that mTOR inhibition can only conceal damage.

retrieval_limits: Some PMC/PubMed web views returned browser challenges or empty content; primary abstracts were retrieved via Europe PMC instead.
Anonymous bucket listing and guessed root-level matrix paths returned 403. Correct public objects under level5/ succeeded without credentials. No access control was bypassed.
A search surfaced another competition repository; it was not used as biological evidence or opened for analysis.
No new systematic adverse-event, drug-label, clinical-trial or competition discussion audit was performed. Existing v21/v24 safeguards and dated requirements remain in force.
